480	It became a byword, and a thorn in the eyes of every hater of Torah
481	in Israel and around the world.
482	But the Sephardic picture is still missing.
483	And the truth is that the fall of the Sephardim was infinitely greater than the fall of
484	the Ashkenazim upon entering Eretz Israel.
485	If the Holocaust struck and cut down the Ashkenazi Torah world,
486	then the Zionists, the erev rav, the leftists, the Mapainiks, call
487	them whatever names you like, damaged the Sephardic Torah world. The problem:
488	In Eretz Israel there was not a single Sephardi from the Eastern communities
489	or Yemen who desecrated Shabbat. There was no such thing. There was no such thing. But
490	deliberate, tendentious actions were carried out by the immigrants
491	here, all kinds of Bolsheviks who came from Russia, haters of
492	religion, who wanted to set the tone and turn everyone who came here into a secular person like them.
493	Anyone who knew what the community of Yemen, Djerba, Baghdad was like, even though the Alliance had already entered
494	a little, you still didn't have an open Shabbat violator who came here to Eretz Israel.
495	They had barely arrived in the country when actions were taken to uproot religion from them,
496	from the Sephardim.
497	It is simple and clear.
498	The Rav of Brisk once said, why did they establish a state?
499	To uproot religion from the people.
500	Let's see you cut peyot in Yemen, if the Yemenite police wouldn't come after you.
501	Let's see you try to sabotage Torah study in Baghdad, if the Iraqi police
502	wouldn't come after you. But when you brought everyone here to Eretz Israel and you set the tone, then
503	no one tells you what to do or how to act. So what happened, gentlemen? They tried
504	to uproot Torah entirely from the Eastern communities and the Yemenites, by force
505	and with brutality, with threats that they wouldn't get food if they ran off to the religious. Over food
506	they starved them if they wanted to keep Torah and mitzvot. They made girls and boys dance, away
507	from their parents, with terrible immodesty. They take a chicken, close the door, bang the
508	chicken against the door and eat it. On Shabbat they go
509	to the orchards, they pick fruit: "See, nothing happened to me, what do you want?"
510	Mass Shabbat desecration. They threatened that they wouldn't get work, and that a school wouldn't
511	get funding if Torah and mitzvot were taught there.
512	They deliberately interfered with their Torah studies.
513	And now you'll say, you feed on all kinds of preachers, demagogues of every sort.
514	No, gentlemen, everything I am telling you now is not even a pinch of what a
515	government commission of inquiry established, which determined everything I am saying now.
516	This was in 1950, January 1950, a government
517	commission of inquiry was established, called the Frumkin Commission.
518	There was a judge, they called him Gad Frumkin, and he was authorized by the commission to go
519	and examine the complaints the immigrants had about secular coercion.
520	About secular coercion.
521	A government commission.
522	Not that today you are investigating what happened 50 or 70 years ago.
523	You are investigating, you are speaking of January 1950. When was the state founded? In '48?
524	You are talking about two years after, two or three years after the founding of the state.
525	That is, things were fresh.
526	They received dozens of testimonies that they were interfered with, that their peyot were cut off,
527	that they were shorn, as it were.
528	Their peyot were cut off, they were forced to desecrate Shabbat.
529	There was enormous pressure on Ben-Gurion and Shazar and their colleagues, who tried to sabotage
530	the commission and its results. It did not help them. The commission
531	was published as an official government report. After taking dozens of testimonies, all these claims
532	were true claims. There was here, beyond any doubt, a tendency to turn everyone secular and to uproot
533	religion from them. It was all in the circles of the Histadrut, under Nachum Levin, who as a result of
534	the report was removed from his post.
535	There is a sentence in Latin, I brought this sentence from the report, I read the whole report
536	to prepare this lesson for you.
537	It is written there, there is a sentence in Latin that says that whoever holds the power
538	determines the religion of the people.
539	So now, since the leftists were the ones who came here
540	at first, they determined the religion of the people and uprooted the Torah from them,
541	and they forced on them what Stalin did not force; they had already completed the job.
542	Why?
543	They could not tolerate the religious, Jewish, exilic, traditional markers.
544	They don't want Jews, they want blind people, they want...
545	a pioneering, renewing, modern, secular state.
546	They could not tolerate any of the religious, traditional, exilic markers.
547	And to our great sorrow, even the Ashkenazi religious were alienated from the Sephardi religious.
548	And so the people of Mapai sensed that the weak link in the chain could be broken.
549	Who was the weak one?
550	The Sephardim.
551	And so whom did they go after?
552	The Sephardim and the Yemenites,
553	the Moroccans and the Djerbans. To cut them off, they transferred some of the children to secular educational institutions,
554	to boarding schools, to secular kibbutzim. They told them, "Your father is old-fashioned, your mother is
555	old-fashioned, now the counselor will teach you." And so it was. They laughed and mocked anyone who kept
556	Torah. One of the greatest scandals in this country is the abduction of the Yemenite children.
557	I'm telling you, people, they put their child, they took him: "Your child is sick," they told them, "he is
558	sick."
559	They took him. I am talking about thousands of babies.
560	Thousands of babies and children, not hundreds.
561	Thousands of babies.
562	They told them, "Your child, your son, is sick, we will take him to a hospital."
563	After two days the parents come to the hospital to visit the child, and they tell them, "He died."
564	What?
565	Where is the body?
566	"We buried him."
567	"Here," they lift up some earth for them, "here he is buried."
568	Do you know what was done here?
569	Do you know what failures there were in this country when it was founded?
570	And what did they do with them? They took them to all kinds of kibbutzim, made them completely secular, and the best part:
571	when their draft time came, suddenly a draft notice arrives at the house.
572	And then the parents understood: "Wow, how did a draft notice arrive at the house?
573	Why doesn't it say in the offices that he died?
574	Apparently he didn't die."
575	Do you know what went on here?
576	Come, I don't have time to get into those links, but understand how much of a tendency there was to uproot religion.
577	There was a lot of naivety, what can I tell you?
578	They believed in simplicity that the State of Israel was the beginning of the Redemption; the great sages of the generation slept with
579	the KKL collection box.
580	Do you know what the Keren Kayemet LeYisrael box is?
581	Sleeping.
582	I still remember that when we were little children, in school they would put this
583	box for us. Do you remember the Keren Kayemet LeYisrael box?
584	A dunam here and a dunam there, clod after clod, Miri Regev.
585	What do you want?
586	They believed.
587	You know, now, from whom did they buy clod after clod?
588	From the Turks, from the Ottomans who ruled here.
589	For years the KKL did not sell land to Muslims.
590	Because when I put in money, I put in money to redeem the land of the people, meaning the people of Israel.
591	There was a petition to the High Court about this: a Muslim petitioned the High Court, saying why doesn't the KKL sell to us?
592	The High Court said he is right, and they began selling to them too.
593	Do you understand what happened?
594	And this is money I put in the box to redeem the land of the people, to buy it from the Turks, and in the end they sell it
595	to the Muslims. So what did we accomplish with that?
596	"What did the sages achieve with their decree?"
597	They arrived in Morocco, gentlemen, and told the people in Morocco, "We will transfer your children
598	first, and afterwards the elders; there's no time to transfer the elders." They came to the parents
599	and told them, "Which yeshiva do you want? We'll take your children."
